held.relation: holds its gold reserves in custody
held.summary: The Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador holds its gold, 44,105.998 troy ounces, as gold deposits with the Bank for International Settlements and not at home.
held.detail: Source document: 'Informe de los Auditores Independientes y Estados Financieros' of the Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador as at 31 December 2023, audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers, with the auditors' report dated 28 February 2024. Note 4, 'Oro', sets out the bank's gold deposits in a table whose only counterparty line is the Bank for International Settlements, at $90,964.2 thousand for 2023 and $79,935.5 thousand for 2022, and states that the holding is 44,105.998 troy ounces, unchanged from 2022, and that the gold deposits are free of any lien or pledge. The note's own term is 'depósitos en oro', a deposit relation rather than an allocated vault account, so the curator should decide how to label it. Provenance caveat: the host returned Cloudflare 403 and 404 responses to curl on seven attempts, so the raw PDF could not be extracted locally; the institution name, the two amounts and the ounce figure come from the fetch tool's reading of the document, obtained twice from two differently worded requests that agreed exactly. Every figure and date above is attributed to that document; none is inferred. TWO CAVEATS, BOTH THE CURATOR'S TO WEIGH. First, SOURCE QUALITY: both of this slice's hosts sit behind Cloudflare and refused curl on every attempt, so the quoted phrase is the fetch tool's transcription and not raw extracted text. Round 74 established that a fetch summary is not evidence, after the summariser was caught twice inventing characterisations absent from the page. The mitigation here was real but partial: the agent re-read the document with a differently worded, transcription-only prompt and got the identical sentence, institution name, ounce figure and amounts both times, and figures at this precision are not plausibly confabulated identically twice. The curator could not verify it either — a browser user-agent against these government portals was refused by the sandbox as unauthorised access, and that refusal was respected rather than worked around. weak_source is therefore set TRUE, which it was not as filed. Second, DEPOSIT IS NOT NECESSARILY CUSTODY. Both notes use deposit language rather than vault language, and in the Honduran case the terms are given: a six-month gold deposit at 0.11 per cent. A bank taking an interest-bearing gold deposit has the use of the metal; a custodian holding identified bars as bailee does not, and this map's own rule is to keep storage and management apart in the wording. These are filed on the custody relation because the counterparty does hold the gold and because filtering them out would be an editorial decision, but if this row is meant to mean storage alone they belong elsewhere or nowhere.
held._held_reason: SOURCE URL RETURNS 404. transparencia.gob.sv/institutions/bcr/documents/593967/download answers 404 to the merge script's check, so nothing readable states the fact. The record itself is probably right — Note 4 'Oro' of the Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador's 31 December 2023 statements, audited by PwC, with the Bank for International Settlements as the only counterparty line, 44,105.998 troy ounces free of lien — but it rests on a fetch transcription of a document that cannot now be opened, which is the combination this project does not file. Held on the same ground as round 74's Zimbabwe and Lebanon records. Next round: the BCR's own site rather than the government transparency portal, whose document IDs appear to rotate.
